correctness.rationale: Conditional emission independence gives E exp(-s A_n)=pi[diag(f_i(s))P]^n 1. Primitive finite-state P ensures a simple Perron eigenvalue 1; the first variation is -h(s) with remainder O(h(s)^2), yielding resolvent ~1/h. The absorbed half-line kernel is nonnegative at site x=1, so Tonelli gives an iff integral of 1/(sqrt(s)h(s)); operational hitting-time decomposition extends fixed x. Under h regularly varying alpha in (0,1), Potter bounds justify rescaling theta_n and give 2x/pi Gamma(1+1/(2alpha))theta_n. Karamata yields the power-log boundary. Independent four finite-state Perron perturbation checks corroborate; infinite asymptotics rely on proof.
